<!-- For someone outside the session: coming to this branch cold, or back to it after a while. It says why the work was done, what is now settled and why, and what is still open, in the words they would use. How each part works and how it got there are in the commit log and the design log, for whoever returns to that part of the game. -->

## What changed

<!-- Why this PR exists, which is most of this section: the goal it served and where the work started (a plan, a report, a playtest). Then, in a paragraph or two, what a player can now do that they could not (for tooling, what an agent session can), as they would notice it rather than how it works: an overview, not an itemization by commit or by feature. A commit is named only where a reader may need to revert it. -->

## Needs a person

<!-- Charter changes, questions of how something feels, and decisions this is waiting on, each as the question with only what it takes to answer it. "Nothing" is an answer. -->

## Played

<!-- How the sittings went, in a sentence: how many, and whether they brought back a lot or a little. Then the few things play changed most, each told as why in a sentence or two: what didn't feel right or wasn't what the person expected, and what was done about it. Not each sitting or each rebuild in turn. If not yet played, what someone playing it should look at. -->

## Measured

<!-- Numbers before and after, and where they were taken. Telemetry, not how it feels. -->

## Verification

<!-- How the final run went: `npm run verify` on the last commit, and CI's result, read after the push. An earlier run is here only if it left something open, such as a failure that went away with no cause found. A failure found and fixed in the ordinary course of the work belongs to the design log. -->

## Not in this PR

<!-- What was left out, or found and not fixed, and why. -->
